provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1962 reads `humilem` where 1862 reads `humiiem`; 1962 reads `meritis` where 1862 reads `meYitis`; 1962 reads `discamus` where 1862 reads `discdmus`; 1962 reads `mundi` where 1862 reads `munai`; 1962 reads `adversantia` where 1862 reads `adversdntia`; 1962 has `cum Deo Patre in unitate.`; 1862 has nothing there; 1862 lower-cases crucis where the 1962 capitalises Crucis, twice; 1862 prints the j-orthography (ejus); 1862 sets a full stop before the conclusion where the 1962 sets a colon; 1862 conclusion is the short cue `Qui vivis et regnas.`; the 1962 writes it out; 1862 layer damages five words (`humiiem`, `meYitis`, `discdmus`, `munai`, `adversdntia`); each is an accent or a serif read wrong and each is unambiguous. Corroboration: 1922 Mame: 16 October is absent from the Mame's own DIE index sweep, and Hedwig was not sought there because the 1862 settles the reading.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui beatam Hedwigem a saeculi pompa ad humilem tuae Crucis sequelam
toto corde transire docuisti: concede; ut ejus meritis et exemplo discamus
perituras mundi calcare delicias, et in amplexu tuae Crucis omnia nobis
adversantia superare: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre in unitate.
